text.p: Whirlpool Corp. Chairman David Whitwam said Tuesday that the company's 23 percent improvement in second quarter earnings is consistent with its expectations for solid performance improvement in 1997.

"Our performance this quarter has been led by significant improvements in our European business, due primarily to our ability to manage costs in a tough economic environment, while strengthening our product mix and improving our margins," Whitwam said in a statement accompanying the results.

North American second-quarter unit shipments were essentially even with last year's record levels, absent a sizable weakness in air conditioner sales caused by cooler than normal weather conditions and high retail inventories carried over from the 1996 season, it said.
Consumer response to new products, particularly Whirlpool brand free-standing ranges and built-in ovens and KitchenAid brand dishwashers, continues to be strong, the company said.

Whirlpool Europe, counter to its industry, showed a slight improvement in second-quarter unit shipments -- sales increased 2.5 percent, in local currency but were down 6.7 percent when translated to U.S. dollars.
Whirlpool said it expects to continue solid year-over-year improvements despite its outlook that full-year 1997 industry shipments will be down slightly from 1996 levels.
The company attributed the European improvement to manufacturing efficiencies in combination with extensive new product introductions.

Latin American sales increased nearly eight percent in the second quarter, driven by higher unit volumes. Even though Brazil's appliance industry slowed from last year's robust levels and competition increased, Whirlpool said it maintained its market share position.

Whirlpool Asia, facing on-going development costs particularly related to Chinese joint ventures, sustained a second-quarter operating loss. The company said it is continuing to address operating issues and its long-term strategy in the region.
